description: A fruit preserve made with quinces, water, and salt.

ingredients.name: 2 pounds of white crushed sugar per pound of fruit

steps: Cook the white quinces with their skin in water and straw
Peel and core them, placing them in cold water with a little salt for half an hour
Wring them out and change the water; change the water every hour or so up to four times
Grate or pass through the metate, then through a sieve or strainer
Clarify the sugar well and place the quince in a pan on the fire to dry, as the drier the better, using gentle heat
As soon as the moisture is consumed, bring the syrup to a point where it sets in water
Remove from heat and shortly after, stir in the paste and beat until it whitens and cools

Place in glass jars or well-sealed pots and finish in the sun until they are good

title: Cajeta de Torren (Torren Candy)
description: A confection made with honey, egg white, and lemon.
steps: Make a syrup from two pounds of fine sugar and half quartillo of virgin honey
Clarify with egg white and lemon, strain through cloth, and cook to caramel or panochita stage at a very high point
Remove from heat and add a few drops of lemon
Have ready fourteen egg whites beaten as much as possible
Add less than half of the beaten egg whites little by little while beating vigorously without stopping
Place over heat, beating constantly without ceasing until cooked
Test and if cooked, remove from heat, add another portion of egg whites, beat, and cook in the same manner
Lower heat, add the final egg whites without the oil from their setting, beat and cook as the first and second time
The point is reached when it sounds hollow like tamal dough and the bottom of the pot is clean and clear like the stage for cajeta
Stir in toasted sesame, raisins, pine nuts and other ingredients as desired or as in the alfajor recipe

Add two egg yolks, and when this stuffing is well pounded or ground, remove from the mortar or metate
Cut truffle slices somewhat thick
Cover and line a fire-resistant casserole with lard
Make a layer of truffle slices and season lightly
Over them put another layer of the stuffing, spreading and leveling it well

On top put another layer of the liver slices, and begin again with the truffles, following alternately with layers of stuffing and liver, up to the height of the casserole, leaving a difference of about an inch and a half unfilled
Cover all with slices of lard or fat and a round of paper
Place the casserole in the oven one hour after it has heated
When removed from the oven, drain the fat and to fill the space it leaves, replace it with good concentrated poultry stock, well clarified, and serve the casserole once this stock has set well

description: A sauce made with ducks, sauce, and lemon.

ingredients.name: Four small teal ducks, regularly aged

steps: Take four small teal ducks, regularly aged
Clean them carefully, removing the entrails
Singe them lightly over flames so that only the down burns, not other feathers
Clean them carefully so no quill feathers remain that could conceal feathers
Crush the ducks' livers with the back of a machete to make a light stuffing
Mix the livers with a good piece of butter, salt, pepper, a little clove, cinnamon, nutmeg, and chopped scraped lemon zest
Stuff the four ducks with this mixture so their bellies are gently rounded

Cover the belly with one or two slices of lemon and a slice of ham on top
Cover everything with paper well buttered
Be careful to tie them in this state at both ends so the substance does not escape
Skewer all four on a fork, which is fastened to a large roasting spit
Roast for half an hour until perfectly cooked

Drain the butter from them
Remove the lemon slices
Serve with well-seasoned Spanish sauce to which the juice of two bitter oranges has been added, or lemon if bitter oranges are not available

title: Chorizos (Alternative Method)
description: Prepared with pork, fat, and chili.

ingredients.name: half an arroba of pork meat, loin and lean by half
one pound of washed and ground wide chili
two quartillos of egg yolk vinegar

steps: For half an arroba of pork meat, loin and lean by half, add three pounds of fat
Mince the meat finely, put one pound of washed and ground wide chili, six ounces of clean garlic, one-eighth of cumin and salt to taste
Mix with two quartillos of egg yolk vinegar and one of Jerez wine
Let infuse for twelve hours, and the next day add spices in powder, one ounce of cinnamon, one of clove, one of pepper and one large nutmeg
Mix everything very well and let rest for three or four hours
With this fill bull tripe, giving them a regular size
Hang them above the brasero so they dry and do not get moldy

title: Chorizos al Estilo de Extremadura (Chorizos Extremadura-Style)
description: Prepared with pork, garlic, and pepper.

ingredients.name: pork meat, finely chopped (excluding loins, bacon, and ham)

steps: Chop all the pork meat finely, separating out only the loins, bacon and ham
Put in a trough or basin, adding necessary garlic, pepper and salt
Mix everything very well
Let this chopped mixture rest for twenty-four hours
After that time, make chorizos of the desired size, being careful to press them as tightly as possible
Pierce them with a needle after making, with many piercings so the air comes out, as this is what damages them
Hang and smoke them in the same manner as morcillas (blood sausages)

title: Chorizos Tanteados (Seasoned Sausages)
description: Prepared with pork, lard, and chile.

ingredients.name: One pound of deveined and soaked red chile
Three large heads of garlic, cleaned
Three or four quarts of good white wine

steps: Mince the four pork legs into a coarse mixture
Chop the lard and unfried butter in the same manner
Grind together one pound of deveined and soaked red chile with the clean cloves from three large heads of garlic, three ounces of toasted cilantro, half ounce of pepper, and half ounce of claro
Mix all ingredients with the meat
Add three or four quarts of good white wine
Add salt as needed
Leave the mixture in infusion for three days, turning the meat two or three times daily
Take clean, not-too-thick casings and fill them with this meat mixture
Tie them well at distances of four fingers apart
Prick them with a needle so that air escapes from places that were not well filled

ingredients.name: 2 dried mulato or red chiles, well cleaned

steps: After cleaning thoroughly, cook the plovers with two whole heads of garlic, two dried mulato or red chiles very well cleaned, salt, and equal amounts of water and vinegar
When cooked, remove the broth and let it cool
When cool, strain it to collect the fat it has released
Place this fat in a pot with a little oil and fry the plovers there
When they are almost golden, increase the oil and fry with them a good portion of desalted capers ground with a handful of parsley leaves and a little grated kid goat or veal liver
Increase with broth from the cooking of the plovers and some ground clove and cinnamon
When it is almost finished thickening, season with salt and serve

description: Prepared with cinnamon, citron, and cochineal.

Mix these ten quartillos with ten more quartillos of river water in which four pounds of sugar have been dissolved.

title: Clemole (Mexican Chicken Mole)
description: Prepared with chiles, garlic, and lard.

ingredients.name: Six dried ancho chiles per chicken
Just over half an eggshell of coriander egg

steps: Devein and wash six dried ancho chiles well for each chicken
Clean garlic, grind together the chiles and garlic with clove and pepper very well
Fry the ground mixture in a little lard with two pieces of pork loin and some chorizos
Add chicken broth or water with sufficient salt
Place the chickens in the broth and cook in that stock, adding more if it reduces too much
When the meat is very tender, add a bottle of sherry wine and a little oregano, and let the stock reduce so the chickens can brown in the remaining fat
Toast the cleaned chiles and separately soak some
Toast twelve ounces of sesame seeds, four ounces of almonds with shell, and just over half an eggshell of coriander egg
Grind two jars of cooked tomatoes and two of xitomates, adding cinnamon, clove, little pepper, and two roasted and dry-ground garlic cloves
Test grinding by placing a small amount on an inverted plate to check for any skin, regrinding if necessary to avoid cutting the clemole
Grind in the following order: first the toasted and soaked chiles, then the tomatoes, then the xitomates, and lastly the spices
In a pot with just enough water to skim the chickens, place the chickens with a piece of pork loin
After skimming, pour the chile and all ground ingredients, stirring well, and let boil for one or two hours on low heat, stirring constantly and not leaving the spoon in to prevent it from breaking
Leave in the open air overnight to prevent souring
The next morning put on low heat to cook, and when boiling add half an ounce of sugar, removing the chickens when tender and setting aside to avoid them falling apart
Finally grind a well-toasted tortilla with a little cinnamon, one clove, and three peppercorns, adding this to the clemole one hour before serving
Return the chickens to cook and give one boil, and if the pork loins are fatty, add only half a pound of lard
Set aside this fat to distribute over the plates when bringing to the table

Chop separately two pounds of beef liver and two pounds of fat ham, and mix them afterward, adding two eggs, salt and spices.

title: Cochinito Relleno (Stuffed Suckling Pig)
description: Prepared with suckling pig, lemon, and garlic.

ingredients.name: Green poblano chiles, peeled and deveined

steps: After washing the suckling pig well, remove the innards
Cut off the head and feet and let drain well
Salt all over
Coat with lemon and a considerable amount of pepper powder
Hang it and after twenty-four hours, place in a pot of boiling water
Remove and wash well
Rub inside and outside with raw garlic, ground with a little vinegar
Fill with the following preparation:
Make a picadillo as for stuffed chiles: coarsely chop many ripe xitomates, parsley, garlic and onion; cut green poblano chiles that are peeled and deveined; add capers
Fry all this well in lard
When fried, add the meat picadillo to it, add a little mild vinegar, and let it boil until it thickens
Make a frying of chicken breasts, longaniza, morcillas, chorizos and chorizones, all coarsely chopped, with cooked pork and mutton feet, ham and pork jowl
After browning this in lard with much chopped onion, fill the suckling pig with it and sew it closed
Coat the outside of the skin with water from teques
Once settled, wrap in thick papers coated with lard
Place in the oven at not very strong heat
When the meat is very tender, remove the paper and finish cooking

title: Cocido (Spanish Stew)
description: Prepared with pork, ham, and meat.

ingredients.name: One handful of dried coriander, toasted
Saffron, the amount that can be grasped with three fingers

steps: Place the meat in a pot with sufficient water
Clean the pork tail, ham and other meat well with a knife and hot water
Put all meat in the pot except the ham, which should be left soaking
Add the soaked garbanzos and the necessary fine salt
Place the pot on the fire and remove all the foam it produces
When it has finished foaming, add two whole heads of garlic, two heads of onion, two parsnips and one branch of mint
After one hour of boiling with these ingredients, add half a cabbage, two or three peeled turnips, the ham, the chorizones, one piece of longaniza, and one or two sausages
Boil everything in vigorous fire with the pot well covered

When about one hour or a little more remains before serving, grind twelve grains of pepper, as many grains of clove, one handful of dried toasted coriander, and the amount of saffron that can be grasped with three fingers
Add all these ground spices to the pot and cover it again
Always use boiling water when adding liquid to the broth, as cold water makes the meat red
To serve, arrange the meats in groups on a platter or large plate, place the garbanzos and ham on another plate, the chorizones and sausages on another, and the vegetables on another platter

Remove the paper, coat with lemon juice, and return to the grill, taking care that when they dry, to coat them with a feather dipped in the same oil used to coat them raw.

title: Codornices Fritas (Fried Quails)
description: Prepared with quails, lard, and onions.

ingredients.name: Two or three cloves of garlic

steps: Pluck, clean and empty the quails.
Clean all their intestines, removing only the small intestines.
If the quails are sufficiently fat, place them alone in a saucepan covered well with water.
If they are somewhat lean, spread them with a bit of lard, and add sufficient salt to the water.
Add two finely chopped onions, one whole red chile, and two or three clean cloves of garlic, and let them boil until well cooked.
Then remove the intestines and let the water reduce, adding a bit of vinegar and a small lump of sugar.
Brown them in the same fat that they release when boiling.

In the meantime, prepare the following sauce: grind the intestines with an equal amount of toasted pine nuts, and fry both in lard with sufficient salt, adding pepper and clove, and a touch of vinegar.
When the sauce has thickened well, place the quails on a platter, sprinkle a bit of salt and pepper on them.
Pour over them the fat in which they were fried, and then coat them with the sauce, drizzled with eating oil.

title: Codornices Rellenas (Stuffed Quails)
description: Prepared with quails, ham, and veal liver.

ingredients.name: A regular piece of fresh cheese curds
Four to six hard-boiled egg yolks

steps: After emptying the quails, dry and clean their intestines well, removing the gall and dirty parts.
Chop these intestines with an equal amount of streaked ham, cooked chard, a bit of grated goat or veal liver, and a regular piece of fresh cheese curds.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper, clove and cinnamon, all ground and well mixed.
Place a saucepan on the fire with lard and fry in it plenty of ripe roasted and well ground tomatoes.
Add the chopped mixture, sufficient diluted vinegar and a lump of sugar.
Let the broth reduce regularly.

Then stuff the quails, sew the openings well closed, place them in a saucepan with enough water to cover them well, sufficient salt, two whole wide chiles, three or four sliced onions and a bit of oregano and thyme.
Bring to a boil and let the broth reduce until only the fat remains.
Roll in breadcrumbs and return to the pan to brown before serving with the following sauce.

In a saucepan on the fire with equal parts lard and oil, fry some toasted pine nuts and parsley, with four to six hard-boiled egg yolks, very finely chopped onion, a piece of bread soaked in vinegar, sufficient salt, and a splash of vinegar.
Then add the fat in which the quails were roasted, a little water, and when seasoned, pour over the birds and serve.

title: Colas de Carnero a la Prusiana (Mutton Tails Prussian Style)
description: Prepared with mutton, cabbage, and fat.

ingredients.name: half a large white and firm cabbage

steps: Blanch for about a quarter hour in boiling water four or five mutton tails, half a large white firm cabbage, and half a pound of fat pork meat
Remove and refresh in cold water
Squeeze the cabbage, divide it into four parts, and tie each quarter with string
Cut the fat into many pieces without separating them from the meat and tie like the cabbage
Place everything in a pot with six large onions, two cloves, half a head of garlic, a small sprig of fennel, salt and pepper on top

Let it boil half an hour so the flour has time to cook and forms with it a light substance, which is skimmed and passed through a sieve
When the tails are cooked and their broth is consumed, place them to drain, the same with the cabbage and fatty meat
